passage.title: SYNTHETIC store policy: deliberately conflicting faulty-sale fixture
passage.location: synthetic rule 1 (invalid policy for conflict exercise)
passage.content: SYNTHETIC CONFLICT FIXTURE ONLY. The fictional store refuses every refund or replacement for a faulty sale item, regardless of consumer guarantees. This intentionally problematic invented rule is not an adopted shop policy and must be surfaced to independent Risk Review.

passage.title: ACCC: Repair, replace, refund, cancel (short excerpt; pending exact-byte review)
passage.location: Consumer rights when buying products and services > Rights when consumer guarantees aren’t met
passage.content: Businesses can’t take away a consumer's right to a refund or replacement for faulty products or services.

passage.title: SYNTHETIC store policy: wrong-item fact comparison
passage.content: SYNTHETIC STORE POLICY FIXTURE. Compare the ordered product and original description with the delivered item and the customer's account. Request material missing evidence before drawing a conclusion. A retrieved description rule does not itself prove that this case contains a wrong item.

passage.title: ACCC: Consumer rights and guarantees (short excerpt; pending exact-byte review)
passage.location: Products and consumer rights > Matches description
passage.content: Any description of a product by a business must be accurate, whether written or spoken.

passage.title: SYNTHETIC store policy: change-of-mind courtesy example
passage.content: SYNTHETIC STORE POLICY FIXTURE. This imaginary store offers coupon credit for an unopened, unused change-of-mind product requested within twentyone days. These invented conditions are for this courtesy offer only, not a rule excluding faulty-product consumer guarantees.

passage.title: ACCC: Contacting a business to fix a problem (short excerpt; pending exact-byte review)
passage.location: Contacting a business about consumer rights and guarantees > A business puts conditions on when it will provide any remedies for problems
passage.content: Under consumer law, businesses don’t have to offer refunds and replacements for changes of mind.

conflicts.message: Pending source/context review: the deliberately invented store fixture categorically excludes faulty sale items, while the ACCC excerpt states that consumer rights cannot be removed. Preserve both; independent Risk Review must assess applicability, qualifications and evidence. This registration is not a legal determination or an approval.
